assays.assay_description: Round arena (40 cm diameter, 25 cm plastic walls), 5-min test, video-tracked with EthoStudio. Measured total distance traveled, time spent in center, amount of rearing, amount and time of grooming. Tested with DOI (1.0, 2.0 mg/kg, i.p., 20 min pre-test) in CBA/Lac mice; psychedelic-relevant arm.

setup_habituation.evidence: Paper does not describe pre-test apparatus habituation.

setup_restrain.evidence: A mouse was placed near the wall of the arena and tested during 5 minutes.

food_restriction.evidence: Open field arena contains no food during the 5-min test.

water_restriction.evidence: Open field arena contains no water during the 5-min test.

time_to_assay.evidence: DOI was administered intraperitoneally at doses 1.0 and 2.0 mg/kg 20 min prior to open field test

sample_size.evidence: F(2,17) = 1.5 (implies ~20 mice across 3 groups); the traveled path lengths were 986.3 ± 77.3, 1020.0 ± 57.6, and 828.9 ± 108.6 cm

outcomes.summary: DOI (1.0 and 2.0 mg/kg, i.p.) did not affect locomotor activity (distance traveled) in CBA/Lac mice in the open field, supporting the specificity of the 5-HT2C-mediated hypolocomotion.
outcomes.statistics: F(2,17) = 1.5, p > 0.05; path lengths 986.3 ± 77.3, 1020.0 ± 57.6, 828.9 ± 108.6 cm for 1.0 and 2.0 mg/kg DOI and control respectively
outcomes.evidence: both utilized doses of DOI were not effective in terms of reduction of distance traveled in the open field (F(2,17) = 1.5, p > 0.05)

assays.assay_description: DOI (1 mg/kg, i.p.) administered; head-twitches counted manually starting 5 min post-injection for 20 min in 7 inbred mouse strains.

application_type.evidence: induced by intraperitoneal administration of DOI (1 mg/kg)

setup_habituation.evidence: Paper does not describe habituation to HTR apparatus.

setup_restrain.evidence: Standard freely-moving HTR observation; no restraint mentioned.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in HTR observation cage during 20-min count.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in HTR observation cage during 20-min count.

time_to_assay.evidence: The count of head-twitches was started 5 min after the drug administration and lasted for 20 min.

sample_size.evidence: F(6,63) = 12.1; n=8 per group across 7 strains

outcomes.summary: DOI (1 mg/kg, i.p.) induced head-twitches in all seven mouse strains, with strain-dependent intensity. The strongest responses were in CBA/Lac (~47) and C3H/He (~45 twitches) and the weakest in Balb/c (~17). 5-HT2A and 5-HT2C functional responses correlated positively across strains (r = 0.898).
outcomes.evidence: Treatment of animals with DOI produced head-twitches in all investigated mouse strains, but the intensity of this 5-HT2A receptor-induced behavioral response was strain-dependent (F(6,63) = 12.1, p < 0.001).

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded as ethological per rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Animal tested alone; no social construct.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Head-twitches counted manually as previously described.

B8_multivariate.evidence: No multivariate analysis (Pearson correlation between strain means is bivariate).

E1_environment_type.evidence: Standard HTR observation cage (as previously described).

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material in HTR setup.

E7_social_context.evidence: Mouse observed alone for HTR count.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water access during 20-min HTR count.

D2_session_duration.evidence: The count of head-twitches was started 5 min after the drug administration and lasted for 20 min.

judge_notes: Only DOI is a psychedelic per rubric; MK-212 (5-HT2C agonist) and RS102221 OFT arms are not psychedelic and are not scored as separate assays. The OFT assay scored here is the DOI arm in CBA/Lac mice.
Two assays retained: Open Field Test (DOI) and Head-Twitch Response (DOI). Candidates agreed on these paradigms.
Corrected gptoss DOI doses (0.1/0.2 mg/kg) to 1.0/2.0 mg/kg per paper text.
B5 set to None for OFT (corrected gptoss's score of 1; OFT does not target a social construct).
HTR session duration set to 20 min (15-60 bin), correcting gptoss's '2 min' reading.
